sentences.text: I want to show you 3 steps to help you become more fluent in English and show you how my Speaking Fluency Club can help you.
Hello, it's Keith from the Keith Speaking Academy, here to help you become a more confident and fluent speaker of English.

Today, I'm going to show you 3 steps to help you become more fluent in English, And also, in the second part of the video, I'll show you my Speaking Fluency Club inside and how that can help you become a much more confident speaker of English.
Let's begin at the beginning.
Okay, this is super simple.
The 3 steps are study, practice, and review.
And these 3 steps make what I call my Speaking Success system.
The first step, study, I actually changed the word for discover.
I think study at times sounds a bit boring.
Discover is much more exciting, like a pirate going across the sea looking for treasure.
You've got that curiosity, you're looking for new language, and to improve, it's about discovering language.
So the first step, discover, is where you discover new vocabulary, new grammar, new ways of saying things.
It's essential input you need, because if you don't learn new words or new grammar, you're always going to say the same things again and again, and you become small but fluent.
And you want to be big but fluent, to have lots of flexibility.
So the first step is to discover new language.
That can be through watching films on Netflix or series or listening to podcasts or watching my live lessons, for example.
Step number 2 is practice speaking.
It's essential, right?
If you want to swim, get in the water.
If you want to speak, practice speaking.
There are 2 ways of doing it.
You can practice on your own, practice with other people.
If you practice on your own, that's great, and that's really good at building confidence and focusing on accuracy.
You can just repeat words or chunks, these kind of collocations.
Just repeat them. Listen and repeat.
It's really good.

And then you can practice putting the words or chunks into little phrases, maybe phrases about you, and that builds your flexibility, but you're making sure you're getting the right pronunciation, the right grammatical form, the right use.
Just little phrases practising on your own.
Bonus tip: record yourself and listen back.
Bonus tip: check with ChatGPT or Claude if you're grammatically correct.
It's really simple.
So, practising on your own is good for accuracy, good for confidence.
However, you also need to practice with other people, because when you practice with other people, the dynamic changes, right?
Suddenly, you've got to listen, You've got to pay attention.
You've got to think of your idea.
You've got to then express the idea in a way and gauge if the other people are understanding you.
It's a lot more complex.
Different ways of doing this.
I mean, obviously, when you're practising with other people, and that can be a classmate, a teacher, doesn't matter really, you can do questions and answers.
That's nice and logical.

You can do problem-solving, you can do a task together, you can do a debate, anything that involves lots of cognitive load where you've got to get the idea, express the idea, and react to other people, right?
All of that is going to really build your speaking fluency.
It kind of takes the language you've learned in step 1, discover, and it's brought it out into the open world where where you're using it, making mistakes, and learning and growing.
Okay?
Step 3 is to review, because if you don't review, you forget.
Simple as that. So you must review.
There are different ways of reviewing.
You can just maybe read or listen again to the original thing you did in step 1.
You could make it more challenging by doing a quiz or a test.
Test yourself. Do you remember the vocabulary?
Do you remember the phrases?
That's another great way of doing it.
You can also review by just having more conversations and doing more practice.
Again, you're kind of recycling the language.
I watched a video recently, it was very, very good, by another YouTuber, and it was about fluency.
And one of the exercises he said, try Answering a question and then give the same answer again, exactly the same answer, and then do it again.
And each time you do it, the first time you've got the idea, the second time you don't need to think about the idea, so you focus on fluency.
The third time you're getting more automatic and you're focusing a lot on fluency, reducing the um, ah, hesitations.
That repeating is so good, and I really like that, and I think that's an important part of the review stage.
So that's it.
That's what I call my Speaking Success System: Discover, Practise, and Review.
And it's a simple path to becoming more fluent in English.
So how can the Speaking Fluency Club help you?
Well, it's designed around the Speaking Success System: Discover, Practise, and Review.
Discover. How do you discover language?
Well, we have live lessons.
Like on my YouTube channel, I have a live lesson first Thursday of the month.
Also in the Speaking Fluency Club, we have these private live lessons, 2 a month.
They last 2 hours, and in there we're in Zoom and I'm presenting language to you.
New language, new words, new collocations, It's also interactive because you have a written chat, you can interact with me.
I do challenge you to think outside of the box and test you a little bit.
But also, in the second part of the live lesson, you get some speaking practice with other students in that live lesson.
So 2 of those a month.
All of that is more input.
Right?
Discovering new language, idioms, vocabulary.
The practice stage comes in the second part of the live lesson, but also the day after the live lesson we have a speaking meeting.
In the speaking meeting, we review the lesson before, and then you're in breakout rooms with other students, small groups, 2 or 3 people, practising speaking on that topic.
In addition to that, at the weekend we have conversation rooms.
Where, again, it's you with 1 or 2 other students on your own.
There's no teacher, but you're just practising speaking, practising fluency based on some questions or activities that get you interacting and speaking, practising building up confidence and fluency.
Then the 3rd step, we have review.
Now, the review, you can go back and watch the recordings of the live lessons, There's a PDF you can download.
There's— at the end of the month, there's a worksheet that reviews all the language we've looked at in that month.
Also, there are tests and little quizzes you can do on the way.

We also have a podcast of all the songs in the live lessons, and you can be listening to that because the songs review all the language that we have learned and studied and discovered in the live lesson.
It's another way to review.
Finally, at the end of the month, I invite you to make a short recording of you speaking on the topic, and I'll give you some feedback.
And it's a great way for you to listen and see your progress month by month, but also to get some personal feedback from me.
So that's the system.
The Speaking Fluency Club, all this discover, practice, review, interaction.
And I guess on top of that, you've really— you're connecting with other people.
So rather than you being on your own, you're meeting other people, students from around the world.
You're exposed to different accents, different cultures.
It's a whole— it's going to open your eyes.
It'll broaden your horizons.
It'll build your tolerance and understanding of other people and how we all communicate in different ways.
It's not just about learning language.
I think you're going to learn a lot more through the Speaking Fluency Club.
It works like a membership, so a bit like Netflix.
So you pay each month.

You can have a look, check it out, see if it's right for you, and I would love to see you inside the Speaking Fluency Club.
If you have any questions, write them down in the comments for this video and I will get back to you and answer them.
That's it for today. Listen, thank you so much for watching.
Welcome to the Speaking Fluency Club.

Bye-bye.
